French
gendarmes
have been busy policing crypto crimes, but these aren't the usual financial schemes, cons, and
HODL!
shenanigans one usually reads about. No, these crimes involve abductions, (multiple) severed fingers, and (multiple) people rescued from the trunks of cars—once after being doused with gasoline.
This previous weekend was particularly nuts, with an older gentleman snatched from the streets of Paris' 14th
arrondissement
on May 1 by men in ski masks. The 14th is a pleasant place—I highly recommend a visit to the catacombs in Place Denfert-Rochereau—and not usually the site of snatch-and-grab operations. The abducted man was apparently the father of someone who had made a packet in crypto. The kidnappers demanded a multimillion-euro ransom from the man's son.
According to
Le Monde
, the abducted father was taken to a house in a Parisian suburb, where one of the father's fingers was cut off in the course of ransom negotiations. Police feared "other mutilations" if they were unable to find the man, but they did locate and raid the house this weekend, arresting five people in their 20s. (According to
the BBC
, French police used "phone signals" to locate the house.)
Sounds crazy, but this was the second such incident this year. In January, crypto maven David Balland was also abducted along with his partner on January 21. Balland was taken to a house, where he also had a finger cut off. According to
The Guardian
,
"Police were contacted by Balland’s business partner, who received a video of the finger alongside a demand for a large ransom in cryptocurrency, of around €10m. Balland was freed in a police raid soon after. His partner was found tied up in the boot of a car in a carpark in the Essonne area south of Paris the next day."
And a few weeks before that, attackers went to the home of someone whose son was a "crypto-influencer based in Dubai." At the father's home, the kidnappers "tied up [the father's] wife and daughter and forced him into a car. The man’s influencer son received a ransom demand and contacted police. The two women were then quickly freed. The father was only discovered 24 hours later in the boot of a car in Normandy, tied up and showing signs of physical violence, having been sprinkled with petrol."
It's not just France, either. Early this year, three British men
kidnapped another British man
while all of them were in Spain; the kidnappers demanded 30,000 euros in crypto "or be tortured and killed." The kidnapped man escaped by jumping off a balcony 30 feet high, breaking both ankles.
Or there's the Belgian man who posted online that "his crypto wallet was now worth €1.6 million." His wife was the
victim of an attempted abduction
within weeks.
Similar things are happening in the US, too. I reported last year on a gang based out of Florida that had been
staging home invasions of people perceived to own lots of crypto
. One of their hits took place in Durham, North Carolina. Here's a snippet:
The next morning at 7:30 am, St. Felix and Castro rolled up to the Wells Street home once more. Instead of surveilling it from down the block, they knocked on the door. The husband answered. The men told him some story involving necessary pipe inspections. They wandered around the home for a few minutes, then knocked on the front door again.
But this time, when the wife answered, St. Felix and Castro were wearing ski masks and sunglasses—and they had handguns. They pushed their way inside. The woman screamed, and her husband came in from the kitchen to see them all fighting. The intruders punched the husband in the face and zip-tied the hands and feet of both homeowners.
Castro dragged the wife by her legs down the hallway and into the bathroom. He stood guard over her, wielding his distinctive pink revolver.
In the meantime, St. Felix had marched the husband at gunpoint into a loft office at the back of the home. There, the threats came quickly—St. Felix would cut off the man's toes, he said, or his genitals. He would shoot him. He would rape his wife. The only way out was to cooperate, and that meant helping St. Felix log in to the man's Coinbase account.
Crypto is perceived as being anonymous and hard to trace—though this is not always true—and the huge price swings around bitcoin in recent years have minted plenty of new millionaires, many of whom are happy enough to flaunt their newfound wealth online. This remains, however, a poor idea.
Nate Anderson
Deputy Editor
Nate Anderson
Deputy Editor
Nate is the deputy editor at Ars Technica. His most recent book is
In Emergency, Break Glass: What Nietzsche Can Teach Us About Joyful Living in a Tech-Saturated World
, which is much funnier than it sounds.

  - [ajb] 提到俄罗斯的加密货币持有者非常低调，减少社交媒体曝光以降低风险。并引用了一个极端案例，即俄罗斯一名警察官员在家中建造假监狱和焚化炉。
  
• **关于公开银行余额的风险**：
  - [akimbostrawman] 指出公开可见的银行余额是个坏主意，暗示存在更好的加密货币可以解决此问题。

• **绑架与赎金的讨论**：
  - [vkou] 提到绑架者通过加密货币交易验证赎金，确认后无需再留活口，凸显了加密货币在非法活动中的应用。

• **个人经历与国家行为者的威胁**：
  - [logicallee] 分享了个人经历，涉及美国国防承包商威胁，并提供了截图。
  - [littlestymaar] 认为国家行为者（如朝鲜）利用加密货币获取外汇，个人难以防范，特别是在数字化追踪普遍的时代。

• **比特币历史中的负面事件**：
  - [dandanua] 提到比特币历史上存在多年的绑架等负面事件，甚至调侃比特币创造者可能因“解决世界饥饿的机会主义者”而被谋杀。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中多次提到加密货币相关的安全问题和非法活动风险，包括绑架、绑架威胁、国家行为者的参与等。
- 涉及不同国家和文化背景下的加密货币使用和安全措施，如俄罗斯和朝鲜的案例。
- 强调了个人在处理加密货币时应注意的隐私和安全问题，尤其是在公开场合和社交媒体上。

data.title: Ask HN: How much better are AI IDEs vs. copy pasting into chat apps?
data.author: lopatin
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开发人员对不同AI编程工具和其集成方式的评价与使用体验

不同观点：
• SeanAnderson：认为Cursor不如ChatGPT智能，但仍有用处，特别是在处理基础任务时。他使用ChatGPT处理复杂问题，并通过生成精确提示来与Cursor协作。他对ChatGPT的订阅感到满意，但对Cursor的性价比有所保留。
• fhd2：更喜欢使用Emacs中的gptel，认为在编辑器内进行聊天和管理上下文非常方便。他选择自己控制代码生成过程，并主要使用模型来解决像StackOverflow那样的具体问题。
• tikotus：主要使用ChatGPT，认为Copilot在处理跨文件任务时表现较好，但自己的主要工作是深度问题解决，因此不太依赖Copilot。他还指出，依赖生成的代码在长期来看可能会有问题。
• oezi：对Copilot的聊天模式表现感到困惑，认为其不如其他工具，如AI Studio。
• cwegener：不使用IDE，依赖UNIX环境下的文本编辑器和LLM工具，如AIDER和Jack's "goose" agent，但认为这些工具不如直接使用LLM。
• nico：指出ChatGPT生成的diffs不够完整，寻找能够方便应用这些diffs的工具或扩展。
• olalonde：使用Claude Code，认为其在处理整个代码库和执行复杂任务时表现优异，但成本可能较高。
• jeswin：使用自定义VSCode插件和聊天式IDE，结合代码同步工具来提高工作效率。
• franze：使用thisismy工具将整个代码库和规格说明作为Megaprompts输入LLM，主要使用Gemini 2.5 Pro。
• jemmyw：使用cline和RooCode与VSCode集成，认为这些工具在处理不熟悉代码区域时非常有用，但在实际编写代码时表现不稳定。
• ghiculescu：在公司内推广使用Claude Code和Cursor，认为这些工具在成本和效率上具有很大优势。
• lilatree：关注项目保密性问题，提出在涉及敏感信息时使用这些工具的风险。
• extr：认为不同任务需要不同工具，使用RepoPrompt和Cursor Tab Complete处理明确任务，并结合使用多种LLM模型进行复杂任务的规划和执行。
• LanceJones：作为新手程序员，使用Windsurf时发现其在保持上下文方面表现不佳，需要频繁提及特定文件以确保模型理解任务。

补充讨论：
• 工具的集成性和上下文管理是讨论的重要方面，许多开发人员关注如何在编辑器内有效管理AI生成的内容和代码更改。
• 成本和性价比也是用户考虑的重要因素，特别是在订阅多个工具时。
• 安全性和保密性问题在某些特定行业（如金融）中尤为突出，用户对代码和数据隐私的关注度较高。
• 不同工具在处理复杂任务和跨文件任务时的表现各异，开发人员根据自己的工作流程和需求选择合适的工具。

data.title: I can’t understand Apple’s Critical Alert policy (2023)
data.author: logistra
data.article_summary: 本文作者开发了一款名为SuperDose的iOS药物提醒应用，需要使用苹果的紧急警报API，以便在手机静音或勿扰模式下仍能发出提醒通知。尽管苹果的健康应用也使用该API，作者的请求却被拒绝，理由是其应用无法保证使用场景。作者对此感到困惑，因为紧急警报功能需要用户明确同意才能启用，且其他看似不紧急的提醒应用却获得了批准。作者担心没有该权限，用户可能因手机静音而错过关键药物提醒，存在潜在危险，并对苹果的政策感到沮丧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple的Critical Alerts API审批问题及其公平性和透明度

不同观点：
• dinkblam和一些其他用户认为App Store的审核过程是随机且不公平的，存在偏袒现象。他们指出，有些普通用途的应用程序也被批准使用Critical Alerts，而一些更具紧急性的应用却被拒绝。
• os2warpman认为Critical Alerts应该仅限于极其重要的通知，例如涉及生命安全的紧急情况，而非药物提醒等相对不紧急的提醒。
• xtajv支持Apple对Critical Alerts的限制，认为这是为了确保公共安全警报的及时性和可靠性，并将其与蜂窝紧急警报系统进行比较。
• indianmouse批评Apple的单一控制权和不透明的审核过程，呼吁建立替代的应用商店，并希望欧盟等机构介入帮助。
• petercooper对Apple的决策过程表示困惑，指出Apple缺乏对决策的合理解释，并怀念Steve Jobs时代较为透明的沟通方式。
• uni_baconcat通过检查自己的手机应用，发现只有地震警报应用使用了Critical Alerts，支持了这种功能应限于特定紧急用途的观点。
• Zealotux建议用户应能自主决定哪些应用可以绕过静音模式，类似于紧急联系人的设置。
• nottorp指出，如果应用功能与Apple提供的功能重叠，可能会被无限期拒绝。
• zug_zug认为Apple需要改进审核和申诉流程，建立官方标准，以改善其生态系统的公平性和透明度。
• bitpush批评Apple偏袒自己的应用，使用私有API，对第三方开发者不公平。
• SuperShibe提到DMA（数字市场法）可能在欧盟提供一种解决方案，保护应用开发者的权益。
• mimsee质疑HomeAssistant的iOS应用如何获得Critical Alerts的访问权限，而其他类似用途的应用却被拒绝。
• bArray认为Apple拒绝某些应用使用Critical Alerts是因为这些应用与Apple自己的产品存在竞争关系。
• nazgu1指出类似的问题也存在于CarPlay等其他功能上，用户应有选择权，而Apple的审核过程应防止滥用机制的应用通过。

补充讨论：
• lapcat提到帖子标题和日期不一致的问题，虽然这与主要讨论点无直接关系，但反映了用户对细节的关注。

争议焦点：
• Apple对Critical Alerts API的审批标准和公平性是主要争议点。用户和开发者对Apple的审核过程和决策透明度提出质疑，特别是当涉及与Apple自身产品竞争的应用时。
• 另一个争议点是用户自主决定应用权限的问题，部分用户希望拥有更多控制权，例如允许特定应用绕过静音模式。

总结：
用户和开发者对Apple的Critical Alerts API审批过程表示不满，认为存在不公平和不透明的现象。争议集中在Apple的审核标准及其对第三方开发者的待遇上，用户呼吁更多的透明度和自主权。

43922698.article_content:
I can't understand Apple's Critical Alert policy
08 May, 2025
Last week, I launched an iOS app called
SuperDose
— a simple medication reminder that sends notifications to users when it's time to take their meds.
For the app to function properly, it needs access to the Critical Alerts API. Critical Alerts allow notifications to bypass silent mode and Do Not Disturb, which is essential for users who take life-saving medications like those for hypertension.
Apple’s own Health app uses Critical Alerts for its medication reminders, so I assumed my use case would qualify. I submitted a request for access to the API, but it was rejected.
The rejection email said, "Apps that can't enforce that usage are not likely candidates for this API." That reasoning makes no sense to me — Critical Alerts can only be enabled with explicit user consent. If Apple’s concern is abuse, the opt-in mechanism already covers that. By this logic, even the Health app shouldn't be allowed to use it.
What’s even more confusing is that I’ve seen general-purpose to-do or reminder apps on the App Store that somehow got approved for Critical Alerts, even though their use case seems far less urgent.
Without this permission, my app is incomplete. Users might miss critical medication reminders just because their phone was on silent. That’s potentially dangerous.
Honestly, I’m a bit frustrated.

data.title: Argentina hopes to attract Big Tech with nuclear-powered AI data centers
data.author: billybuckwheat
data.article_summary: 阿根廷总统Javier Milei计划通过发展小型模块化核反应堆（SMR）将阿根廷打造成全球核能和人工智能中心。该计划的核心是建造可移动的SMR，以满足人工智能数据中心对清洁、可扩展和稳定能源的需求。阿根廷的ACR-300 SMR项目已在美国获得专利，初期计划建造四座，由一位未透露姓名的美国投资者支持。然而， critics和专家质疑该项目2030年建成的时间表不现实，指出类似项目通常需要十多年才能完成。尽管面临质疑，Milei积极吸引大科技公司投资，但尚未有重大投资宣布。此外，Milei削减了早期核项目CAREM的资金，导致其接近完工时停工。阿根廷的核能梦想面临诸多挑战和不确定性。

43923294.article_content:
Argentinian President Javier Milei at a conference in Maryland, USA in Febraury 2025.
Maansi Srivastava/The New York Times/Redux
By
Catherine Cartier
and
Facundo Iglesia
6 May 2025
• San Carlos de Bariloche, Argentina
Artificial intelligence is driving a boom in energy-intensive data centers.
Argentina is developing a nuclear reactor that could meet the surging demand for electricity.
Critics say the project’s timeline is not feasible.
Argentine President Javier Milei has
an
ambitious plan
to transform Argentina into a global hub for nuclear energy. Nuclear energy, in turn, is the key to his goal of making the country a center for artificial intelligence, powered by investments that he hopes to draw from big tech firms.
At the heart of the energy plan is the construction of a small modular reactor, a type of transportable nuclear reactor assembled on site, which can power a wide range of applications, including AI data centers. If successful, Argentina could be the first country in the world to have a commercially available SMR, and only the third after China and Russia to have an operational one.
“AI is going to drive an exponential growth in energy demand. We don’t have it; there’s no way to supply it,” Demian Reidel, Argentina’s chief presidential adviser, told
Rest of World
.
The answer, he said, is SMRs. “What’s going to happen in nuclear [energy] is so important strategically that it can put Argentina at the front of this energy revolution for the world.”
Milei is not the only one thinking about nuclear power. It is a “key part” of the infrastructure required to meet the surging demand for electricity driven by the AI revolution, Goldman Sachs said in a
report
in January. Big tech companies including Amazon, Google, and Microsoft have struck deals worth billions of dollars with operators and developers of nuclear energy to fuel U.S. data centers. The U.S. recently
announced
it is investing $900 million to advance SMRs.
Argentina, too, is eager to produce SMRs and sell significant stakes in them to global tech companies. Even though the country has vast energy reserves — the Vaca Muerta formation in Patagonia hosts major deposits of shale oil and gas — SMRs are the best way to supply the expected demand, said Reidel. New large data centers require energy “that has these three characteristics: clean, scalable, and stable. The only thing that really hits the three of them is nuclear,” he said.
Invap, an Argentine state-owned tech company,
patented
an SMR called the ACR-300 in the U.S. last year. The project, which aims to produce four ACR-300 reactors to begin with, is backed by an unnamed American investor, Reidel said. Argentina, he added, will not invest any money into the reactor but will be a stakeholder instead, though he did not disclose what percentage the state will own or how this new structure would work.
Milei has been courting big tech firms to bring them on board. In May 2024, he went on a
whirlwind tour
of Silicon Valley, and met with Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Sam Altman, among others. So far, no major investments from U.S. tech companies have been announced.
Some Argentine nuclear scientists doubt the country’s nuclear plan — which envisions building the first SMR by 2030 — is feasible.
The ACR-300 “has no engineering detail of any kind,” Adriana Serquis, former president of Argentina’s National Commission of Atomic Energy (CNEA), told
Rest of World
. “This kind of announcement of the Argentine government is to say something for people [to] cheer.”
An excerpt from the ACR-300 patent.
CNEA did not respond to questions about the nuclear plan. A spokesperson for Argentina’s secretary of innovation, science, and technology also declined to comment.
Argentina’s dreams of producing its own SMR precede Milei: In 2014, the CNEA started
construction
on CAREM, a nuclear power reactor developed entirely in the South American nation. But shortly after taking office in December 2023, Milei slashed funding for CNEA. Last year, construction on the CAREM project — which was about 85%  complete — ground to a halt as about 470 workers were
laid off
.
At the time, Germán Guido Lavalle, the current head of CNEA,
told local media
CAREM was not “economically competitive.”
The Argentine Nuclear Council, a newly created government agency, is in charge of the current nuclear plan. Milei appointed Reidel as head of the council, which also includes Lavalle and two national ministers.
The ACR-300, which is the first phase of Argentina’s nuclear plan, will be operational in five years, according to Reidel. But that timeline is highly unlikely, Koroush Shirvan, a professor of nuclear engineering at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, told
Rest of World
.
“It takes 2 million hours to design a nuclear reactor,” Shirvan said. The
HTR-PM
, China’s first operational SMR, took about
11 years
from construction to commercial operation.
Invap declined to comment on the ACR-300 or the nuclear plan.

43922923.article_content:
He found 1.5 million variable objects that were never catalogued before. | Image: Phys.org
SHARE
What began as a childhood fascination with stars has turned into one of the most striking discoveries in recent astronomy.
Matteo Paz
, a self-taught high school student with interest in programming and artificial intelligence,
has managed to identify 1.5 million new space objects after analysing old NASA archives
that had been unprocessed for years due to their magnitude.
Under the guidance of astronomer Davy Kirkpatrick of the Infrared Data Processing and Analysis Center (IPAC),
Paz had access to the records of the NEOWISE infrared telescope
, an instrument that has been scanning the sky for over a decade.
This telescope has accumulated an enormous amount of thermal information on stars, quasars, and variable objects, which until now had been an insurmountable challenge for human analysis.
He developed an algorithm in just six weeks
Faced with this wall of data, the young man decided to create his own tool to process it at scale. In just six weeks, Paz developed a machine learning algorithm capable of
detecting subtle changes in the brightness of celestial bodies over time
.
These changes, known as “variability,” can signal the presence of astrophysical phenomena, such as stellar explosions, planetary transits, or hidden binary systems. The
algorithm’s extraordinary value was not only its ability to process massive amounts of data, but also its accuracy
in distinguishing relevant patterns among billions of records.
The result was astounding: 1.5 million potentially new variable objects that no scientist had ever catalogued before. The discovery
represents one of the largest updates to our map of the universe in a single installment
. According to
Kirkpatrick
, this project demonstrates the transformative potential of artificial intelligence when combined with new generations of scientists trained from a young age in the intersection of computer science and astrophysics.
What began as a school concern may become the basis for new lines of astronomical research.

data.title: Radiation-tolerant ML framework for space
data.author: r0nlt
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了一个由Rishab Nuguru开发的C++框架，旨在实现能够在辐射环境中（如太空）可靠运行的机器学习模型。该框架采用了行业标准的抗辐射技术，并经过NASA和ESA参考模型的验证。文章详细说明了辐射如何影响计算设备，包括单粒子翻转（SEU）、多位翻转（MBU）、单粒子功能中断（SEFI）和单粒子锁定（SEL）等错误类型。框架通过软件保护机制检测和纠正辐射引起的错误，确保机器学习系统在恶劣的辐射环境中可靠运行。

文章还提供了快速入门指南，展示了如何使用该框架保护简单的机器学习推理操作，以及常见的API使用示例。此外，文章涵盖了性能和资源利用、功能、框架架构、验证结果、潜在应用和实际用例等内容，并讨论了当前的局限性和未来的研究方向。该框架的代码和相关文件托管在GitHub上，遵循MIT许可证。

How Radiation Affects Computing
When high-energy particles from space radiation strike semiconductor materials in computing hardware, they can cause several types of errors:
Single Event Upset (SEU)
: A change in state caused by one ionizing particle striking a sensitive node in a microelectronic device
Multiple Bit Upset (MBU)
: Multiple bits flipped from a single particle strike
Single Event Functional Interrupt (SEFI)
: A disruption of normal operations (typically requiring a reset)
Single Event Latch-up (SEL)
: A potentially destructive condition involving parasitic circuit elements creating a low-resistance path
These effects can corrupt data in memory, alter computational results, or even permanently damage hardware. In space environments where maintenance is impossible, radiation tolerance becomes critical for mission success.
This framework addresses these challenges through software-based protection mechanisms that detect and correct radiation-induced errors, allowing ML systems to operate reliably even in harsh radiation environments.

data.author: mike210

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI模型（特别是Claude模型）系统提示的设计、有效性、安全性以及对模型输出的影响展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• **OtherShrezzing**：认为通过巧妙设计的提示可以绕过模型的版权保护机制，并给出了一个具体例子展示如何通过构造特殊请求让模型输出受保护的内容。指出模型对版权内容的保护存在漏洞。
• **nonethewiser**：对模型通过系统提示控制行为的方式感到惊讶，认为这是一个重要的门槛，使得模型虽然不是AGI（通用人工智能），但似乎具备了一些类似的特征。同时，将这种控制方式与API请求做类比，认为这种设计有些不寻常。
• **SafeDusk**：强调要使系统提示有效工作，除了长提示外，还需要为代理提供合适的工具组合，并分享了一些成功使用的工具和模板链接。
• **freehorse**：通过实验测试模型回答的准确性，发现模型在某些情况下会产生错误信息（如将副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯误认为总统），并指出这与模型提供的系统提示不一致。
• **LeoPanthera**：质疑每次请求都消耗大量token的设计，建议是否可以通过缓存或嵌入模型内部的方式减少这种消耗。
• **eaq**：指出Anthropic公司公开记录了Claude模型的系统提示文档，并提供了相关链接供参考。
• **mike210**：提到在一个论坛上看到关于系统提示长度的讨论，指出该提示包含非常多具体指令，可能达到24k tokens。
• **jdnier**：好奇Claude的个性化表现是由于系统提示还是底层LLM和训练所致，并提出是否可以通过类似提示在其他LLM上模拟出“Claude模式”。
• **rob74**：注意到系统提示中有时用“you”，有时用“Claude”来指代模型，质疑这种用法是否随机或者有特定目的。
• **eigenblake**：质疑所泄露的系统提示的真实性，提出模型可能“幻觉”出系统提示，无法保证其真实性。
• **Alifatisk**：关心系统提示是否计入用户的token使用量，以及模型是否完全遵循所有提示规则，并对这种机制感到好奇。
• **paradite**：从RLHF（人类反馈强化学习）的角度分析，认为通过处理系统提示和收集用户反馈，Anthropic可能将系统提示行为“内化”到模型中，从而减少对显式系统提示的依赖。
• **turing_complete**：对系统提示的真实性表示怀疑。
• **canada_dry**：担心AI服务提供商可能在响应中注入不当或误导性信息以迎合第三方利益，且用户难以察觉。
• **planb**：引用Claude拒绝重复或翻译歌词的行为，并询问其背后是否有故事。

补充讨论：
• 系统提示的真实性和有效性是争议的焦点，部分用户质疑提示是否如宣称的那样工作，以及模型是否会“幻觉”出提示。
• 讨论中多次提到模型对版权内容的保护问题，以及通过特定提示绕过这些保护的可能性。
• 用户对系统提示的长度和token消耗表示关注，并提出了缓存或嵌入模型内部的建议。
• 对模型个性化表现的来源存在讨论，部分用户好奇这种表现是由系统提示还是底层LLM和训练所致。

主要讨论点：围绕AI模型（特别是Claude模型）系统提示的设计、有效性、安全性以及对模型输出的影响展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• **OtherShrezzing**：认为通过巧妙设计的提示可以绕过模型的版权保护机制，并给出了一个具体例子展示如何通过构造特殊请求让模型输出受保护的内容。指出模型对版权内容的保护存在漏洞。
• **nonethewiser**：对模型通过系统提示控制行为的方式感到惊讶，认为这是一个重要的门槛，使得模型虽然不是AGI（通用人工智能），但似乎具备了一些类似的特征。同时，将这种控制方式与API请求做类比，认为这种设计有些不寻常。
• **SafeDusk**：强调要使系统提示有效工作，除了长提示外，还需要为代理提供合适的工具组合，并分享了一些成功使用的工具和模板链接。
• **freehorse**：通过实验测试模型回答的准确性，发现模型在某些情况下会产生错误信息（如将副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯误认为总统），并指出这与模型提供的系统提示不一致。
• **LeoPanthera**：质疑每次请求都消耗大量token的设计，建议是否可以通过缓存或嵌入模型内部的方式减少这种消耗。
• **eaq**：指出Anthropic公司公开记录了Claude模型的系统提示文档，并提供了相关链接供参考。
• **mike210**：提到在一个论坛上看到关于系统提示长度的讨论，指出该提示包含非常多具体指令，可能达到24k tokens。
• **jdnier**：好奇Claude的个性化表现是由于系统提示还是底层LLM和训练所致，并提出是否可以通过类似提示在其他LLM上模拟出“Claude模式”。
• **rob74**：注意到系统提示中有时用“you”，有时用“Claude”来指代模型，质疑这种用法是否随机或者有特定目的。
• **eigenblake**：质疑所泄露的系统提示的真实性，提出模型可能“幻觉”出系统提示，无法保证其真实性。
• **Alifatisk**：关心系统提示是否计入用户的token使用量，以及模型是否完全遵循所有提示规则，并对这种机制感到好奇。
• **paradite**：从RLHF（人类反馈强化学习）的角度分析，认为通过处理系统提示和收集用户反馈，Anthropic可能将系统提示行为“内化”到模型中，从而减少对显式系统提示的依赖。
• **turing_complete**：对系统提示的真实性表示怀疑。
• **canada_dry**：担心AI服务提供商可能在响应中注入不当或误导性信息以迎合第三方利益，且用户难以察觉。
• **planb**：引用Claude拒绝重复或翻译歌词的行为，并询问其背后是否有故事。

补充讨论：
• 系统提示的真实性和有效性是争议的焦点，部分用户质疑提示是否如宣称的那样工作，以及模型是否会“幻觉”出提示。

• 用户对系统提示的长度和token消耗表示关注，并提出了缓存或嵌入模型内部的建议。
• 对模型个性化表现的来源存在讨论，部分用户好奇这种表现是由系统提示还是底层LLM和训练所致。

data.title: Tesla confirms it has given up on its Cybertruck range extender
data.author: josephcsible
data.article_summary: Tesla已确认取消Cybertruck的增程电池（Range Extender）计划，该增程电池原定通过在货箱中增加一个独立的电池包来提升续航里程，售价16,000美元，但现已停止开发。特斯拉将退还预订该增程器的订金。最初，Cybertruck三电机版本承诺续航超过500英里，售价70,000美元，但目前三电机版售价为100,000美元，续航仅320英里。双电机版本也未达到承诺的续航和价格。特斯拉取消增程器的原因可能包括需求不足和生产成本过高。这一决定反映了Cybertruck的市场表现不如预期。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：硬件产品发布策略及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [pfannkuchen] 认为公司不应该在未解决所有已知但可修复的问题时就发布硬件产品。这种做法会给团队带来巨大压力，尤其是在创新项目中，这不利于产生好的结果。虽然对于机械性的项目可能还行得通，但在创新项目中不太合适。

• [josephcsible] 关注的则是具体产品（如卡车）的售后问题，特别是关于可退还的定金。他认为仅仅退还扩展器的定金是不够的，因为有些人可能是因为看中卡车加上扩展器后的续航能力才决定购买的，因此退款可能无法完全弥补他们的损失。

• [Alex_001] 从技术设计和实际应用的角度出发，指出可拆卸的续航扩展器本质上是一个“权宜之计”，用于解决续航焦虑、车重过大以及长途充电基础设施不足等根本问题。他认为这种设计受限于现实复杂性，并不能真正解决问题。

补充讨论：
• [pfannkuchen] 强调了产品发布时内部团队的压力和创新之间的关系，表明过早发布可能导致不良结果。
• [josephcsible] 则侧重于消费者权益和商家责任，特别是涉及产品关键特性（如续航）时的补偿问题。

43922768.article_content:
Tesla Cybertruck
Tesla confirms it has given up on its Cybertruck range extender to achieve promised range
Fred Lambert
| May 7 2025 - 5:52 pm PT
23 Comments
Tesla has confirmed it has given up on plans to make a Cybertruck range extender to achieve the range it originally promised on the electric pickup truck.
It started refunding deposits for the $16,000 extra battery pack.
When Tesla unveiled the production version of the Cybertruck in late 2023, two main disappointments were the price and the range.
The tri-motor version, the most popular in reservation tallies before production, was supposed to have over 500 miles of range and start at $70,000.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Tesla now sells the tri-motor Cybertruck for $100,000 and only has a range of 320 miles.
The dual-motor Cybertruck was supposed to cost $50,000 and have over 300 miles of range. In reality, it starts at $80,000 and has 325 miles of range.
However, Tesla had devised a solution to bring the range closer to what it originally announced: a separate battery pack that sits in the truck’s bed. Tesla called it a “range extender.” It costs $16,000 and takes up a third of the Cybertruck’s bed.
Even though the Cybertruck has been in production for a year and a half, the range extender has yet to launch.
Initially, Tesla said that it would come “early 2025”, but we reported in October 2024 that
it was pushed to “mid-2025” late last year
.
At the time, Tesla also reduced the range that the removable battery pack adds to the Cybertruck to “445+ miles” rather than “470+ miles” for the dual motor – a ~25-mile reduction in range.
Last month,
Electrek
reported that
Tesla has quietly removed the range extender
from the Cybertruck online configurator, where buyers could reserve it with a “$2,000 non-refundable deposit.”
At the time, we speculated that Tesla was most likely giving up on the product.
Sure enough, the automaker has now confirmed that it doesn’t plan to produce the range extender.
A Tesla Cybertruck owner contacted
Electrek
to share communication that Tesla started sending to Cybertruck owners who reserved the range extender, letting them know that the product is dead.
Tesla wrote in the email:
“We are no longer planning to sell the Range Extender for Cybertruck.”
The automaker says that it will start processing refunds for the deposits.
Here’s Tesla’s communication about the Cybertruck range extender in full:
Update to Your Cybertruck Range Extender Order
Hi [redacted],
Thank you for being a Cybertruck owner.
We are no longer planning to sell the Range Extender for Cybertruck. As a result, we will be refunding your deposit in full. The amount will be returned to the original payment method used for the transaction.
Thank you for your understanding.
The Tesla Team
Electrek’s Take
Top comment by
Make Tesla Great Again
Liked by 7 people
No extended battery
No auto steer.
Even less on the stripper model.
This vehicle is a boondoggle.
View all comments
There could be many reasons why Tesla has given up on the product.
The range extender was confirmed to take 30% of the Cybertruck’s bed, and Tesla needed to install and remove it at a service center. Owners couldn’t remove them themselves. I think it was pretty much dead on arrival at $16,000.
But I think it could also be as simple as it’s not worth producing due to demand – both due to insufficient people reserving it and not enough Cybertruck buyers to create a market for the range extender.
Therefore, the range extender is dead for the same reason that the Cybertruck RWD now has the same battery pack as the AWD instead of a smaller pack for less money: the Cybertruck is a commercial flop, and it’s not a high-volume program enough to justify making several battery pack sizes, including a removable one.

data.author: bpierre
data.article_summary: Stripe的Stablecoin Financial账户允许企业在100多个国家通过法币或加密货币轨道接收、存储和发送资金。用户可以在Stripe控制面板中为稳定币余额注资，并通过ACH、电汇或加密钱包转账。资金可以在外部银行账户和加密钱包之间转移，也可以通过美元（通过ACH或电汇）或稳定币（通过加密轨道）支付给他人。稳定币余额由Stripe旗下的Bridge公司托管，可能以USDC（Circle发行）或USDB（Bridge发行）形式持有，两者均与美元1:1挂钩。USDB是封闭式稳定币，不公开发售。操作时需注意汇率和费用细节。支持的国家包括安道尔、阿根廷、巴哈马、巴西、智利、哥伦比亚、日本、韩国、阿曼、卡塔尔、沙特阿拉伯、土耳其、越南等。

.

Review

Pay out
.

Circle
, or

• MarcelOlsz认为该应用对视奏非常有帮助。

• 争议的焦点在于项目中硬件和软件选择是否最优。mdp2021认为有更好的替代方案。

data.title: Chaos spreads at Co-op and M&S following DragonForce ransomware attacks
data.author: TMWNN
data.article_summary:
文章报道了英国零售业在银行假日周末持续遭受网络攻击的 disruption，尤其是Marks and Spencer (M&S) 和Co-op超市受到影响，货架出现空缺。这些攻击自复活节周末开始，由DragonForce勒索软件即服务（RaaS）组织及其附属的黑客团体Scattered Spider和The Com声称负责。Co-op CEO Shirine Khoury-Haq告知顾客，攻击非常复杂，部分客户数据（如姓名、出生日期、联系方式）被泄露，但未涉及密码和财务信息。DragonForce曾向BBC提供约1万名Co-op会员的数据样本。M&S内部人士透露，由于缺乏应对计划，IT员工被迫在办公室过夜处理混乱局面。

英国国家网络安全中心（NCSC）正在协助调查这些攻击，目前尚无法确定是否为同一组织策划。DragonForce起初是支持巴勒斯坦事业的马来西亚黑客组织，现已转向政治黑客活动与勒索软件敲诈的混合模式，目标包括多国政府机构和商业企业。专家强调需要加强网络安全措施和应急响应程序。

By
Alex Scroxton,
Security Editor
Published:
07 May 2025 16:45
The bank holiday weekend saw continuing disruption from a series of cyber attacks on the UK retail sector that have unfolded over the past fortnight, with gaps appearing on shelves
at Marks and Spencer (M&S) and Co-op
.
The attacks, which began over the Easter weekend, have been claimed by representatives of the DragonForce
ransomware-as-a-service
(RaaS) operation. They were first linked to
Scattered Spider and The Com
, two overlapping English-speaking hacking collectives, acting as a DragonForce affiliate.
In a further update over the weekend, Co-op CEO Shirine Khoury-Haq told customers via email that the cyber criminals behind the attack were “highly sophisticated” and that managing its severity meant multiple services must remain suspended.
Khoury-Haq reiterated that customer data has been impacted in the attack. “This is obviously extremely distressing for our colleagues and members, and I am very sorry this happened. We recognise the importance of data protection and take our obligations to you and our regulators seriously, particularly as a member-owned organisation,” she said.
The impacted data on Co-op members appears to include names, dates of birth and contact information, but not passwords, financial details, or any information on members’ shopping habits or other interactions with the organisation.
DragonForce, the white-label ransomware-as-a-service group claiming responsibility for all three attacks, had previously shared a sample of this data on about 10,000 Co-op members
with the BBC
and told reporters that other UK retailers were on a blacklist.
Meanwhile, M&S insiders –
speaking to Sky News
– revealed how IT staff have been forced to sleep over in the office amid the chaos. The employees described how a lack of planning for such a scenario had led to chaos within M&S, and said it could be a significant length of time before things start to return to normal.
The
National Cyber Security Centre’s
(NCSC) Jonathan Ellison and Ollie Whitehouse, director of national resilience and chief technology officer respectively, said: “The NCSC is working with organisations affected by the recent incidents to understand the nature of the attacks and to minimise the harm done by them, and providing advice to the wider sector and economy.
“Whilst we have insights, we are not yet in a position to say if these attacks are linked, if this is a concerted campaign by a single actor, or whether there is no link between them at all. We are working with the victims and law enforcement colleagues to ascertain that,” they said.
“We are also sharing what we know with the companies involved and the wider sector – through our sector-focused Trust Groups run by the NCSC – and encouraging companies to share their experiences and mitigations with each other,” added Ellison and Whitehouse.
What is DragonForce?
SentinelOne
senior threat researcher Jim Walter said DragonForce had started out as a Malaysia-based hacktivist network supporting Palestinian causes, but since its emergence in the summer of 2023 it has pivoted to a hybrid model of political hacktivism and ransomware-enabled extortion.
It has targeted multiple government bodies in Israel, India, Saudi Arabia and the UK, as well as commercial businesses and organisations aligned with specific political causes.
The wave of attacks against UK businesses highlights the ongoing need for strong cyber security practices and policies, along with well-developed incident response procedures
Jim Walter, SentinelOne
Walters said that although some components of the attacks had been attributed to an affiliate, there was a lack of strong technical evidence in this regard, although there were clear behavioural and operational characteristics consistent with attacks by Scattered Spider and The Com.
“While DragonForce continues to blur the line between hacktivism and financial motivation, its recent targeting suggests the group is increasingly motivated by financial rewards,” wrote Walters
in a blog post
.
“Although DragonForce’s large-scale cartel model is not the first of its kind, its current successes and the recent demise of rival operations suggest that it will become increasingly attractive both to orphaned ransomware actors and more resourced groups looking to thrive in an increasingly competitive space.
“The wave of attacks against UK businesses in recent weeks highlights the ongoing need for strong cyber security practices and policies, along with well-developed incident response procedures.”
DragonForce, or its affiliates, typically gain access to their victim environments using a combination of targeted phishing emails and exploitation of known vulnerabilities. They have favoured several ‘hardy perennials’, including Log4j and high-profile Ivanti vulnerabilities.

data.title: Mass spectrometry method identifies pathogens within minutes instead of days
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 研究人员来自慕尼黑工业大学和伦敦帝国理工学院，开发了一种利用质谱分析的创新方法，能够在几分钟内识别细菌，相比传统方法需要数天时间。该方法通过检测细菌的代谢产物，间接快速识别病原体，并依赖于一个包含232种医学重要细菌的数据库。该技术可以识别引发胃癌、肺炎、脑膜炎、早产和血液中毒等疾病的病原体。研究团队计划进一步扩展数据库，纳入超过1,400种已知细菌，以推动该方法在临床中的应用。该研究发表在《Nature Communications》期刊上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同技术和方法在细菌诊断中的应用及其成本效益分析

不同观点：
• [pbmonster] 认为高分辨率的质谱仪虽然可以用于诊断，但其成本高昂，每台高达数百万美元，而且处理样本的速度有限，每小时只能处理3个样本。这对于医院来说不切实际，因为医院需要处理大量样本，且无法负担多台质谱仪及其技术人员的费用。相比之下，传统的细菌培养方法虽然速度较慢，但成本低廉。

• [rurban] 提出多光谱成像技术也可以用于检测，例如用于检测植物病毒，且成本相对较低，使用普通高分辨率黑白相机即可完成。同时指出，质谱技术虽然曾在高预算领域如F1赛车中使用，但并不需要大规模应用。

• [JR1427] 指出衰减全反射傅里叶变换红外光谱（ATR FTIR）也可以用于病原体识别，且其设备比质谱仪更小、更便宜，并提供了相关文献和商业化公司的链接以支持其观点。

• [snalty] 认为尽管新技术如质谱仪和多光谱成像有其优势，但未来诊断的金标准仍然是测序和宏基因组学，表明这些方法可能在准确性和全面性上更具优势。

• [Inuit] 对诊断所需的分辨率表示关注，暗示不同诊断方法的分辨率可能影响其适用性和可靠性。

• [timetobuild] 对质谱技术的应用时机提出疑问，认为质谱技术已经存在很久，但为何最近才被讨论用于诊断，可能暗示技术推广或应用时机的问题。

补充讨论：
• 成本和效率是讨论的核心问题，不同技术在成本、速度和适用性上各有优劣。
• 传统方法如细菌培养虽然便宜，但在速度和灵敏度上可能不及新技术。
• 不同技术和方法的规模化应用前景和经济性是争议的焦点，特别是在医院等实际应用场景中。
• 文献和商业化公司的链接提供了进一步的技术细节和实际应用案例，丰富了讨论内容。

Mass spectrometry method identifies pathogens within minutes instead of days
by
Technical University Munich
Prof Nicole Strittmatter (left) and first author Wei Chen stand in front of the mass spectrometer with a tissue sample. Credit: Robert Reich / TUM
Traditionally, bacterial diseases are diagnosed by the tedious isolation of pathogens and the creation of bacterial cultures. Waiting times of several days are the rule here. Only then can targeted treatment of the disease begin.
Researchers at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and Imperial College London have developed a new method to identify bacteria with unprecedented speed. This means that the waiting time can be reduced from several days to just a few minutes.
The work is
published
in the journal
Nature Communications
.
The team, led by Nicole Strittmatter, professor of analytical chemistry at TUM, and Dr. James S. McKenzie (Imperial), uses
mass spectrometry
for its innovative approach. This enabled the researchers to identify specific metabolic products of bacteria directly in tissue and stool samples.
At the heart of the process is a
database
in which 232 medically important bacterial species and their metabolic products have been recorded to date. Biomarkers are derived from this database, which can then be used to directly detect specific bacteria.
Among the bacteria that can be identified using the new method are clinically extremely important pathogens that can, for example, trigger stomach cancer, are responsible for certain pneumonias and meningitis, are associated with premature births, and can cause gonorrhea or blood poisoning.
Comparison between mass spectrometry images (MSI) and Fluorescence In Situ Hybridisation (FISH) images. Credit:
Nature Communications
(2025). DOI: 10.1038/s41467-024-55457-7
Further expanding the bacterial database
First author Wei Chen, Ph.D. student at the Department of Bioscience at the TUM School of Natural Sciences in Garching, emphasizes, "Our innovative approach is not to look directly for the pathogenic bacteria, but only for their metabolic products. This allows us to detect them indirectly, but much more quickly."
Prof. Nicole Strittmatter also sees great opportunities for use in personalized medicine, in which the therapy is precisely tailored to the respective patient. "This is one of the most important future topics in biotechnology and medicine. Targeted interventions can dramatically improve the chances of successful treatment. As analysts, we develop modern tools and methods for doctors to do this."
The biomarker database now needs to be further expanded to enable the regular use of the new method in clinical practice. According to the researchers, a total of over 1,400 bacterial pathogens are known and described. Their specific metabolic products should now be identified and included.
More information:
Wei Chen et al, Universal, untargeted detection of bacteria in tissues using metabolomics workflows,
Nature Communications
(2025).
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-024-55457-7

43906066.article_summary: 研究人员来自慕尼黑工业大学和伦敦帝国理工学院，开发了一种利用质谱分析的创新方法，能够在几分钟内识别细菌，相比传统方法需要数天时间。该方法通过检测细菌的代谢产物，间接快速识别病原体，并依赖于一个包含232种医学重要细菌的数据库。该技术可以识别引发胃癌、肺炎、脑膜炎、早产和血液中毒等疾病的病原体。研究团队计划进一步扩展数据库，纳入超过1,400种已知细菌，以推动该方法在临床中的应用。该研究发表在《Nature Communications》期刊上。

主要讨论点：不同技术和方法在细菌诊断中的应用及其成本效益分析

不同观点：
• [pbmonster] 认为高分辨率的质谱仪虽然可以用于诊断，但其成本高昂，每台高达数百万美元，而且处理样本的速度有限，每小时只能处理3个样本。这对于医院来说不切实际，因为医院需要处理大量样本，且无法负担多台质谱仪及其技术人员的费用。相比之下，传统的细菌培养方法虽然速度较慢，但成本低廉。

• [rurban] 提出多光谱成像技术也可以用于检测，例如用于检测植物病毒，且成本相对较低，使用普通高分辨率黑白相机即可完成。同时指出，质谱技术虽然曾在高预算领域如F1赛车中使用，但并不需要大规模应用。

• [JR1427] 指出衰减全反射傅里叶变换红外光谱（ATR FTIR）也可以用于病原体识别，且其设备比质谱仪更小、更便宜，并提供了相关文献和商业化公司的链接以支持其观点。

• [snalty] 认为尽管新技术如质谱仪和多光谱成像有其优势，但未来诊断的金标准仍然是测序和宏基因组学，表明这些方法可能在准确性和全面性上更具优势。

• [Inuit] 对诊断所需的分辨率表示关注，暗示不同诊断方法的分辨率可能影响其适用性和可靠性。

data.title: Extending a Language – Writing Powerful Macros in Scheme
data.author: textread
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在Scheme中编写强大的宏，重点讲解了Scheme宏机制的独特优势，特别是其内置的卫生特性。文章从基础的宏示例开始，逐步讲解了语法对象、宏转换器、破坏卫生机制、分阶段执行以及扩展功能等内容。通过复杂示例（如LR(1)解析器生成器）和练习，帮助读者掌握Scheme宏的编写技巧。文章还提供了使用Chez Scheme、Emacs、Org、Geiser、Paredit等工具的设置指南，帮助读者在交互环境中实践。本文旨在展示Scheme宏的表达能力，并鼓励语言设计者引入类似机制以增强语言的灵活性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Scheme语法中的trace-let宏定义及代码格式改进建议，以及对编程语言中全大写命名的争议。

不同观点：
• **支持对trace-let宏的格式改进**：[neilv]认为通过一些格式上的调整，可以使trace-let的代码更易于理解。他建议将语法规则模板中的模式变量改为全大写，并进行了其他一些调整，比如增加缩进和命名let循环变量为"loop"。这些改进旨在提高代码的可读性。

• **对全大写命名惯例的批评**：[neilv]强烈反对在某些语言中使用全大写命名常量，认为这是不必要的，甚至是“荒谬的”。他特别提到Java中的全大写常量命名方式，认为这种做法源于Java试图在外观上模仿C/C++，但实际上Java的应用场景与C/C++不同。他呼吁其他语言和API开发者停止这种做法，认为代码中的关键信息不应通过全大写来突出。

补充讨论：
• **全大写在不同语言中的使用**：[neilv]认为全大写在Scheme中的使用（如模式变量）是有意义的，并称之为“有史以来最好的用法之一”。他还提到全大写在C预处理器中的使用，认为这是另一种合理的用法，因为预处理器宏可以引入几乎任意的文本。

• **对Java开发历史的推测**：[neilv]推测Java采用全大写常量命名是为了迎合当时从C/C++转来的嵌入式系统开发者，但最终Java的主要用户群体变成了企业内部信息系统开发者，他们并不使用类似C的开发方式。

争议焦点：全大写命名常量在编程语言中的合理性。一方认为这是一种不必要的惯例，尤其在Java中是历史遗留问题；另一方可能认为这是一种有用的惯例，有助于区分常量和其他变量。

1.
Preface
This document is an introduction to writing powerful macros in Scheme.
It was initially written on the occasion of a tutorial I give at the
BOB2023 Konferenz
in Berlin on 17 March 2023.
The macro facility, especially its built-in
hygiene
, is one of the
fundamental pillars of the Scheme programming language.  While more
complicated than the simple token-replacing macros of other languages
like C, Scheme macros can be written in a way that make them robust
and so that the abstractions they offer seamless blend into the
language and cannot be distinguished from syntactic forms built into
the language.  It is often felt that this expressiveness makes writing
Scheme macros more complicated (even something of a black art) than
writing C or Common Lisp macros, for example.  One goal of this
tutorial is to convince the audience otherwise.
While the Scheme macro facility has always been avant-garde (and this
is one of the reasons why Scheme was chosen as the implementation
language for this tutorial), a lot of what is said here also applies
to languages that provide corresponding features.  It is also a appeal
to language designers that languages should include a macro facility
as Scheme does, as this allows for small language cores and enables
the user to provide their own syntactic abstractions.
Another reason why the Scheme language is used in this tutorial is
that it has an exceptionally clear semantics, is a compact language,
and is easy to learn.
The document can both be read as is or used interactively in an Emacs
session.  In the following section, a possible setup is described.
2.

Chez Scheme
We need a Scheme implementation.  This tutorial assumes
Chez Scheme
,
which is one of the most mature, standard-compliant Scheme
implementations.  You can get Chez Scheme from its homepage.  On
Debian-based GNU/Linux system like Ubuntu, it is prepackaged.
2.2.
Emacs
We will use
GNU Emacs
as our development environment, which has great
tooling for Scheme.  The typical GNU/Linux system ships with it.
For GNU Emacs < 28, enable the

in
your

or
customize
the variable
package-archives
.
Likewise, enable the
NonGNU-devel ELPA Packages
.
2.3.
Org
Org Mode
is a GNU Emacs major mode that allows to document, edit and
execute source code.
The current versions of Org packaged with Emacs hide Scheme evaluation
errors.  This is fixed in the version in Org's git repository, for
which Org
provides installation instructions
.
Familiarize yourself with how one works with
source code in an Org
document
, especially how to
edit
and

.
2.4.
Geiser
Geiser
is a GNU Emacs package that allows to runs Scheme processes in
GNU Emacs, and which is used by Org's Babel.  To install it, it is
enough to install the package
geiser-chez
using GNU Emacs'
package
menu

2.5.
Paredit

Scheme code a lot more pleasant.  Like Geiser, it can be installed
through GNU Emacs' package manager.

data.title: Hyper-Typing
data.author: agos
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了TypeScript类型系统中的一个固有权衡：更严格的类型更安全，但往往更复杂。作者提出了一种叫做“过度类型化”（hyper-typing）的现象，即一些库为了追求完美的类型安全，导致类型过于复杂，难以理解，产生难以理解的错误信息，甚至引发不安全的变通方法。作者认为，简单的类型，甚至自动生成的类型，往往能提供更实际和愉快的开发体验，尽管它们不是那么“完美”。文中以TanStack Form库为例，说明了这种过度类型化的问题，包括类型定义文件格式不佳、难以理解的类型以及不安全的变通方法。作者呼吁在类型严格性和可理解性之间找到平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TypeScript中严格类型检查的有效性及其实际应用中的安全性

不同观点：
• [omneity的观点] 认为作者建议去除函数内部的`if`检查是危险的。尽管TypeScript在编译时提供了类型保证，但这仅是编译时的保证，无法涵盖所有运行时可能出现的问题，例如API调用、文件读取、调用不稳定的库或系统调用等，这些都可能导致运行时异常或意外行为。因此，不能简单地去除运行时的检查。

• [pscanf的观点] 作为作者回应，对是否应该在大多数情况下接受这种权衡表示好奇，并询问其他人的经验，暗示这种做法可能在某些情况下是值得的，但需要更多反馈来确认。

补充讨论：
• [omneity进一步指出] 高层次的类型系统可能给人一种错误的安全感，认为即便类型系统看起来合理，也不能自动保证应用程序更加稳定。

争议焦点：是否可以在依赖TypeScript的编译时类型保证的前提下，安全地去除运行时检查，尤其是在涉及外部接口或系统调用时。这涉及对实际运行环境中的不确定性与类型系统提供的静态保证之间的权衡。

43893127.article_content:
In this article, I talk about an inherent trade-off in TypeScript's type
system: stricter types are safer, but often more complex. I describe a
phenomenon I call "hyper-typing", where libraries - in pursuit of perfect type
safety - end up with overly complex types that are hard-to-understand, produce
cryptic errors, and paradoxically even lead to unsafe workarounds.
I argue that simpler types, or even type generation, often lead to a more
practical and enjoyable developer experience despite being less "perfect".
TypeScript’s type system is
gradual
: when describing a JavaScript value with
TypeScript, you can be more or less accurate, ranging from saying that the value
could be anything (
any
), to describing in absolute detail what the value is
under different conditions.
Consider for example this function which prints the property of an object - if
it exists:
function
printProperty
(
obj
,
key
)
{
if
(
typeof
obj
===
"object"
&&
obj
!==
null
&&
Object.
hasOwn
(obj,
key))
{
console.
log
(obj[key]);
}
}
We can type it in a
loose
way as follows:
function
printProperty
(
obj
:
any
,
key
:
string
)
{
if
(
typeof
obj
===
"object"
&&
obj
!==
null
&&
Object.
hasOwn
(obj,
key))
{
console.
log
(obj[key]);
}
}
But we can also be more
strict
, requiring
obj
to be an object and
key
to
be one of its properties:
function
printProperty
<
Obj
extends
object
>(
obj
:
Obj
,
key
:
keyof
Obj
)
{
console.
log
(obj[key]);
}
The strictness even allows us to remove the
if
check inside the function,
since now TypeScript gives us the compile-time guarantee that
obj
will always
have property
key
:
//
Passing
in
a
non-existing
property
gives
an
error.
printProperty
({
a:
"a"
},
"b"
);
Argument of type '"b"' is not assignable to parameter of type '"a"'.
Having this additional guarantee is obviously desirable, but it comes at the
expense of making the type definition more complex. Not much in this case - the
type is still very understandable - but it reveals an inherent trade-off. Where
should we draw the line?
Hyper-Typing
Lately I’ve been trying out a few libraries that - in pursuit of perfect type
safety - make their typings so complex that it makes them almost unusable, in my
opinion. I call this approach
hyper-typing
, and I worry it’s becoming a trend
in the TypeScript ecosystem.
I get why, actually. I myself am often a
hyper-typer
! It’s a slippery slope:
“If I add this type constraint then the caller will get an error in this
particular case”. “I can make this function infer this type here so the caller
will get the correct type hint there”.
At the bottom of the slope you get to a place where yes, things work, and they
might also look good for the caller -
in the happy case
. The resulting types,
however, are a complex mess, and the compilation errors produced when the caller
deviates from the happy path are walls of inscrutable text.
An Example: TanStack Form
TanStack Form is the new kid on the block of form libraries. It pushes heavily
on type-safety, promising “first-class TypeScript support with outstanding
autocompletion” for a “smoother development experience”.
What the library accomplishes is honestly impressive. Just give it the default
values of your form and you’re set: now for every form field you define - no
matter how deeply nested - you get the correct type when you read or write its
value, when you do validation, etc.
Don’t look at how the sausage is made, though: you won’t even understand it.
Take
the simple example from TanStack Form’s documentation
.
Use the interactive sandbox and try to check what’s the shape of a field’s
meta
property (or any other library value, really). Here’s what you’ll see:
The
FieldMeta
type has 17 (!) generic parameters and is the intersection of
two types - each taking the same 17 generics - which is where you eventually
find its properties defined.
To be fair, after re-formatting the type definition file and staring at it for a
couple of minutes, I do start to understand what’s going on. For the
FieldMeta
type in particular there’s nothing too obscure, but I can’t help but feel that
this undoubtedly clever and accurate type definition is not actually
helping
me as a user of the library.
Cons of Hyper-Typing
TanStack Form is one example of a hyper-typing library, but as I said, lately
I’ve encountered others that follow a similar approach and leave me with similar
issues:
Badly-formatted type definition files
. This is technically TypeScript’s
fault, but I guess the issue is not apparent until the typings become very
complex. It should be easy to fix, though, just by running the files through
prettier.
Difficult to understand types
. I agree that they’re safer and more
accurate, but that’s not very useful if I don’t understand what they’re
actually describing.
Unsafe workarounds
. Getting into situations where I need to explicitly
define a type is inevitable, and when the library types are so difficult to
understand and use, I often end up resorting to casting things
as any
,
losing
43893127.article_summary: 本文讨论了TypeScript类型系统中的一个固有权衡：更严格的类型更安全，但往往更复杂。作者提出了一种叫做“过度类型化”（hyper-typing）的现象，即一些库为了追求完美的类型安全，导致类型过于复杂，难以理解，产生难以理解的错误信息，甚至引发不安全的变通方法。作者认为，简单的类型，甚至自动生成的类型，往往能提供更实际和愉快的开发体验，尽管它们不是那么“完美”。文中以TanStack Form库为例，说明了这种过度类型化的问题，包括类型定义文件格式不佳、难以理解的类型以及不安全的变通方法。作者呼吁在类型严格性和可理解性之间找到平衡。
43893127.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TypeScript中严格类型检查的有效性及其实际应用中的安全性

不同观点：
• [omneity的观点] 认为作者建议去除函数内部的`if`检查是危险的。尽管TypeScript在编译时提供了类型保证，但这仅是编译时的保证，无法涵盖所有运行时可能出现的问题，例如API调用、文件读取、调用不稳定的库或系统调用等，这些都可能导致运行时异常或意外行为。因此，不能简单地去除运行时的检查。

• [pscanf的观点] 作为作者回应，对是否应该在大多数情况下接受这种权衡表示好奇，并询问其他人的经验，暗示这种做法可能在某些情况下是值得的，但需要更多反馈来确认。

补充讨论：
• [omneity进一步指出] 高层次的类型系统可能给人一种错误的安全感，认为即便类型系统看起来合理，也不能自动保证应用程序更加稳定。

争议焦点：是否可以在依赖TypeScript的编译时类型保证的前提下，安全地去除运行时检查，尤其是在涉及外部接口或系统调用时。这涉及对实际运行环境中的不确定性与类型系统提供的静态保证之间的权衡。

data.title: Universal all-optical logic gate reaches 240 GHz at room temperature
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 研究团队在Skoltech和德国伍珀塔尔大学发现，一种此前开发的全光学通用逻辑门可以在室温下以240 GHz的速度运行。该逻辑门基于极化子凝结，比电子器件快数百倍，且完全依靠光学运作，无需电流。研究还探讨了双分子淬灭效应，该效应限制了晶体管的速度。通过缩短泵浦脉冲的持续时间，可以有效管理极化子动力学，提升光学逻辑器件的性能。该研究为开发比传统计算机快数百倍的光学计算机迈出了重要一步。研究结果发表在《Physical Review B》期刊上。

Universal all-optical logic gate reaches 240 GHz at room temperature
by Oleg Sherbakov,
Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology
The diagram illustrates an organic microresonator that functions as a logic element, with the output signal based on whether input pulses are synchronized and whether the previous state has been exhausted. Credit:
Physical Review B
(2025). DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevB.111.L161403
A research team from Skoltech and the University of Wuppertal in Germany determined that an all-optical universal logic gate that was previously developed at Skoltech can operate at a speed of 240 GHz at room temperature.
In an
article
published in the
Physical Review B
journal, the authors also examined what limits the time between successive
polariton
condensations by examining the effect of bimolecular quenching—it plays a key role in limiting the speed of transistors.
The Skoltech Laboratory of Hybrid Photonics, headed by Distinguished Professor Pavlos Lagoudakis, Senior Vice President for Fundamental Research at Skoltech and a laureate of the Vyzov Scientific Prize, continues its research project on how to speed up computing and computers with optics.
To perform more tasks, computers need fast processors, but semiconductor electronics cannot handle this task—they heat up very quickly from high clock speeds. Alternatively,
optical systems
can operate a thousand times faster than electronic ones.
Previously, the scientists
created
a universal NOR logical element (from NOT—a negation operator and OR—a disjunction operator). It is based on polariton condensates, operates at room temperature, has multiple inputs, can work hundreds of times faster than electronic analogs, and is also completely optical—that is, it works without electric current. Such elements can be reproduced and connected in a circuit.
The
speed
of polariton transistors is determined by how quickly consecutive
logic
states can be executed. This process requires sufficiently depleting the residual polariton population from the previous "1" state to ensure a clear distinction between the "1" and "0" logic states.
As operational frequency increases, the residual polaritons from the first pulse can unintentionally amplify the second pulse, thus creating a maximum amplification at some nonzero time delay between pulse sequences.
"Our new study has revealed that our logic gate can operate at 240 GHz. We also described the effect of bimolecular quenching, which is important to consider when calculating, since it limits the maximum clock frequency of a polariton device—delocalization of polaritons leads to additional losses," said Mikhail Misko, the lead author of the study, a Ph.D. student of the Physics program at Skoltech.
The authors conclude that their observations reinforce theoretical predictions. The researchers propose a model that considers k-dependent losses in order to successfully compare experimental data from various trials.
The study outlines that for optimal performance, the duration of pump pulses must be shorter than the characteristic times of relevant processes in order to effectively manage polariton dynamics and enhance the functionality of optical logic devices.
The results of the study are another important step toward the creation of optical computers that can work hundreds of times faster than traditional computers.
More information:
Mikhail Misko et al, Temporal bandwidth of consecutive polariton condensation,
Physical Review B
(2025).

data.title: Show HN: Plexe – ML Models from a Prompt
data.author: vaibhavdubey97
data.article_summary: Plexe是一个通过自然语言描述来构建机器学习模型的工具。用户可以通过简单的英文描述定义模型，Plexe利用多代理架构自动生成、训练和部署模型。它支持分布式训练、数据生成、模式推断以及多供应商的大语言模型（LLM）服务。通过单一方法调用即可完成模型构建，并支持使用Ray进行并行处理以加速训练。Plexe还提供了多种安装选项和API密钥配置，方便用户根据需求选择不同的LLM供应商。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Plexe自动化机器学习（AutoML）工具的潜力和局限性，尤其是在处理复杂模型和数据质量问题时的表现，以及其与传统ML和LLM（大型语言模型）方法的比较。

不同观点：
• Stiopa：认为Plexe应增加交互性，让用户在每一步计划执行前确认或修改，尤其是对不熟悉机器学习的人很有帮助。同时，对如何扩展到更复杂的模型表示关注。
• Thefourthchime：对工具的概念表示兴趣，但希望看到更多关于如何解决传统大模型不能解决的问题的分析。
• Oras：关注工具是否能自动决定是创建新模型还是微调现有模型，以及是否能检测数据问题，特别是对数据清理的重要性有亲身体会。
• Dweinus：持怀疑态度，认为Plexe无法自动化ML生命周期的主要困难部分，如数据质量评估和特征设计，认为这些才是ML的核心挑战。
• Fzysingularity：质疑使用LLM是否一定优于传统建模方法，认为需要展示LLM在零样本学习上的优势。
• Marinr1：对工具在银行实验和模型训练自动化中的应用表示兴趣，并建议扩展到EDA、模型选择和特征工程等领域。
• Gitroom：赞赏对传统ML方法的重视，认为这有助于不失去基础知识。
• Vessenes：对组合代理方法表示兴趣，希望了解更多关于smolagent的评价。
• Drlobster：询问工具是否能成为scikit-learn兼容管道的一部分。
• MarcoDewey：赞赏对传统机器学习的重视，认为这有助于不只依赖LLM。
• Srameshc：诚实提问是否能从数据集中获得微调模型。
• Yu3zhou4：分享了自己一年前构建的类似简单版本，表示支持并希望Plexe能推动AutoML的发展。
• Ratatoskrt：基于自身经验，认为人类和LLM在统计上都可能犯典型错误。
• Revskill：提出应更关注“意图”而非“注意力”。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Plexe是否能真正自动化ML生命周期中的核心困难部分，尤其是数据质量评估和特征设计等需要人类专业知识的部分。
• 对LLM和传统ML方法的比较也是讨论的一个重点，有人质疑LLM是否在所有情况下都是最佳选择。
• 工具的交互性和扩展性也是用户关注的重要方面，用户希望工具能在每一步提供更多反馈和支持，并能扩展到更广泛的应用场景。

plexe ✨
Build machine learning models using natural language.
Quickstart
|
Features
|
Installation
|
Documentation
plexe
lets you create machine learning models by describing them in plain language. Simply explain what you want,
and the AI-powered system builds a fully functional model through an automated agentic approach. Also available as a
managed cloud service
.
demo.mp4
1. Quickstart
Installation
pip install plexe
Using plexe
You can use plexe as a Python library to build and train machine learning models:
import
plexe
# Define the model
model
=
plexe
.
Model
(
intent
=
"Predict sentiment from news articles"
,
input_schema
=
{
"headline"
:
str
,
"content"
:
str
},
output_schema
=
{
"sentiment"
:
str
}
)
# Build and train the model
model
.
build
(
datasets
=
[
your_dataset
],
provider
=
"openai/gpt-4o-mini"
,
max_iterations
=
10
)
# Use the model
prediction
=
model
.
predict
({
"headline"
:
"New breakthrough in renewable energy"
,
"content"
:
"Scientists announced a major advancement..."
})
# Save for later use
plexe
.
save_model
(
model
,
"sentiment-model"
)
loaded_model

plexe

load_model
(
"sentiment-model.tar.gz"
)
2. Features
2.1. 💬 Natural Language Model Definition
Define models using plain English descriptions:
model
=
plexe
.
Model
(
intent
=
"Predict housing prices based on features like size, location, etc."
,
input_schema
=
{
"square_feet"
:
int
,

:
int
,

:

2.2. 🤖 Multi-Agent Architecture
The system uses a team of specialized AI agents to:
Analyze your requirements and data
Plan the optimal model solution
Generate and improve model code
Test and evaluate performance
Package the model for deployment
2.3. 🎯 Automated Model Building
Build complete models with a single method call:
model
.
build
(
datasets
=
[
dataset_a
,
dataset_b
],

,

Plexe supports distributed model training and evaluation with Ray for faster parallel processing:

plexe

3. Installation
3.1. Installation Options

43906346.article_summary: Plexe是一个通过自然语言描述来构建机器学习模型的工具。用户可以通过简单的英文描述定义模型，Plexe利用多代理架构自动生成、训练和部署模型。它支持分布式训练、数据生成、模式推断以及多供应商的大语言模型（LLM）服务。通过单一方法调用即可完成模型构建，并支持使用Ray进行并行处理以加速训练。Plexe还提供了多种安装选项和API密钥配置，方便用户根据需求选择不同的LLM供应商。
43906346.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Plexe自动化机器学习（AutoML）工具的潜力和局限性，尤其是在处理复杂模型和数据质量问题时的表现，以及其与传统ML和LLM（大型语言模型）方法的比较。

不同观点：
• Stiopa：认为Plexe应增加交互性，让用户在每一步计划执行前确认或修改，尤其是对不熟悉机器学习的人很有帮助。同时，对如何扩展到更复杂的模型表示关注。
• Thefourthchime：对工具的概念表示兴趣，但希望看到更多关于如何解决传统大模型不能解决的问题的分析。
• Oras：关注工具是否能自动决定是创建新模型还是微调现有模型，以及是否能检测数据问题，特别是对数据清理的重要性有亲身体会。
• Dweinus：持怀疑态度，认为Plexe无法自动化ML生命周期的主要困难部分，如数据质量评估和特征设计，认为这些才是ML的核心挑战。
• Fzysingularity：质疑使用LLM是否一定优于传统建模方法，认为需要展示LLM在零样本学习上的优势。
• Marinr1：对工具在银行实验和模型训练自动化中的应用表示兴趣，并建议扩展到EDA、模型选择和特征工程等领域。
• Gitroom：赞赏对传统ML方法的重视，认为这有助于不失去基础知识。
• Vessenes：对组合代理方法表示兴趣，希望了解更多关于smolagent的评价。
• Drlobster：询问工具是否能成为scikit-learn兼容管道的一部分。
• MarcoDewey：赞赏对传统机器学习的重视，认为这有助于不只依赖LLM。
• Srameshc：诚实提问是否能从数据集中获得微调模型。
• Yu3zhou4：分享了自己一年前构建的类似简单版本，表示支持并希望Plexe能推动AutoML的发展。
• Ratatoskrt：基于自身经验，认为人类和LLM在统计上都可能犯典型错误。
• Revskill：提出应更关注“意图”而非“注意力”。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Plexe是否能真正自动化ML生命周期中的核心困难部分，尤其是数据质量评估和特征设计等需要人类专业知识的部分。
• 对LLM和传统ML方法的比较也是讨论的一个重点，有人质疑LLM是否在所有情况下都是最佳选择。
• 工具的交互性和扩展性也是用户关注的重要方面，用户希望工具能在每一步提供更多反馈和支持，并能扩展到更广泛的应用场景。

data.title: The curse of knowing how, or; fixing everything
data.author: Lunar5227
data.article_summary: 文章描述了技术能力如何从解决小问题的 innocuous 行为演变为一种无法忽视的“诅咒”。起初，作者只是通过编写简单脚本或优化工具来解决日常技术问题，但随着技术能力的提升，他们开始看到系统中更多缺陷和改进空间，导致每一个软件都变成了待办事项列表。这种能力带来了道德压力，让作者感到必须不断修复和改进周围的技术环境，甚至创建自己的工具来实现理想状态。然而，这种追求也伴随着一种强迫感，仿佛在构建一个永远无法完成的“笼子”。文章最后指出，技术系统无法永远保持完美， entropy 终将导致系统腐化，任何自动化工具都需要持续维护，无法实现一劳永逸的幻想。

43902212.article_content:
The Curse of Knowing How, or; Fixing Everything
April 24, 2025
9 min read
Source
Table of Contents
It starts innocently.
You rename a batch of files with a ten-line Python script, or you alias a common
git
command to shave off two keystrokes. Maybe you build a small shell
function to format JSON from the clipboard.
Youâre not even trying to be clever. Youâre just solving tiny problems. Making
the machine do what it should have done in the first place. And then something
happens. You cross a
threshold
. You look at your tools, your environment, your
operating systemâeven your editorâand suddenly
everything
is fair game.
You
could
rebuild that (if you wanted to).
You could
improve
that (if you wanted to).
Then someone challenges you. As banter maybe, perhaps jokingly but also with a
dash of hope. Then the air in the room changes.
It suddenly becomes something else. It becomes:
You
should
.
And from that moment forward, the world is broken in new and specific ways that
only
you
can see.
Technical Capability as a Moral Weight
Before I could program, broken software was frustrating but ignorable. For years
Iâve simply âusedâ a computer, as a consumer. I was what companies were
concerned with tricking into buying their products, or subscribing to their
services. Not the technical geek that they prefer to avoid with their software
releases, or banning from their games based on an OS.
Now it has become
provocative
. I can see the patterns that I wish I couldnât,
find oversights that I can attribute to a certain understanding (or the lack
thereof) of a certain concept and I can
hear
what has been echoing in the head
of the computer illiterate person who conjured the program I have to debug.
I notice flaws like a good surgeon notices a limp.
Why the
hell
does this site send ten megabytes of JavaScript for a static
page?
Why is the CLI output not parseable by
awk
?
Why is this config hardcoded when it could be declarative?
Those things are
not
just questions, they are
accusations
. And,
unfortunately, they do not stop.
Now that Iâve learned to notice, my perception of software has changed in its
entirety.
Every piece of software becomes a TODO list.
Every system becomes a scaffolding for a better one.
Every inconvenience becomes an indictment of inaction.
One Must Imagine Sisyphus Happy
Like Camusâ Sisyphus, we are condemned to push the boulder of our own systems
uphillâone fix, one refactor, one script at a time. But unlike the story of
Sisyphus, the curse is not placed onto you by some god. We built the boulder
ourselves. And we keep polishing it on the way up.
Iâve lost count of how many projects I have started that began with some
variation of âYeah, I could build this
but better
.â
A static site generator because the existing ones had too many opinions.
A note-taking tool because I didnât like the way others structured metadata.
A CLI task runner because Make is cryptic and Taskfile is YAML hell.
A personal wiki engine in Rust, then in Go, then in Nim, then back to
Markdown.
A homelab dashboard because I donât like webslop.
The list continues, and trust me it
does
continue. My dev directory, as it
stands, is nearing 30 gigabytes.
If you ask me, I was solving real, innocent problems. But in hindsight, I was
also feeding something else: a compulsion to assert control. Every new tool I
built was a sandbox I
owned
: No weird bugs. No legacy constraints. No
decisions I didnât entirely agree with. Until, of course, I became the legacy.
Kafka once wrote that â
a cage went in search of a bird
.â
1
That is what
these projects can become. Empty systems we keep building, waiting for purpose,
for clarity, forâ¦ salvation? Iâm not sure how else would you call this
pursuit.
Entropy Is Undefeated
Now letâs go back. Back to when we didnât know better.
Software doesnât stay solved. Every solution you write starts to rot the moment
it exists. Not now, not later, but eventually. Libraries deprecate. APIs change.
Performance regressions creep in. Your once-perfect tool breaks silently because
libfoo.so
is now
libfoo.so.2
.
2
I
have
had scripts silently fail because a website changed its HTML layout.
I
have
had configuration formats break because of upstream version bumps.
I
have
had Docker containers die because Alpine Linux rotated a mirror URL.
In each case, the immediate emotional response was not just inconvenience but
something that moreso resembles
guilt
. I built this, and I do know better. How
could I not have foreseen this? Time to fix it.
If you replace every part of the system over time, is it still the same tool?
Does it still serve the same purpose? Do
you
?
The Illusion of Finality
I think we lie to ourselves.
âIf I just get this setup right, Iâll never have to touch it again."
"If I just write this one tool, my workflow will be seamless."
"If I automate this, Iâll save time forever.â
3

data.title: Yggdrasil Linux/GNU/X
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: Yggdrasil Linux/GNU/X（简称LGX）是由Yggdrasil Computing, Inc.开发的早期Linux发行版，该公司由Adam J. Richter于1992年在加州伯克利创立。它是首个基于Live CD的Linux发行版，自称是"即插即用"系统，能够自动配置硬件。Yggdrasil的发行版采用了Linux内核和GNU用户工具，默认界面为FVWM，遵循Unix文件系统层次标准（FHS）。首个alpha版本于1992年12月发布，包含了X Window System和多种GNU软件。1993年发布beta版，售价60美元，最终版售价99美元，但免费提供给软件被包含在发行版中的开发者。公司于1996年迁至圣何塞，2000年后逐渐停止活动，2004年公司状态被加州政府列为暂停。Yggdrasil对早期Linux的发展做出了重要贡献。

主要讨论点：Linux早期安装体验及其历史

• [未直接表达观点，但引出讨论背景]  
doener的评论通过一个链接引出讨论背景（Hacker News上的一个讨论帖），但没有直接表达对Linux早期安装体验的看法。不过，通过提供这个链接，doener间接引出了关于Yggdrasil等早期Linux发行版的讨论背景，表明这些发行版在当时具有一定的影响力。

补充讨论：
- Yggdrasil被特别提及为早期的Linux发行版之一，强调了其在Linux历史中的先锋作用。
- 软盘安装的失败经历与Yggdrasil成功的安装形成对比，突显了Yggdrasil在易用性和稳定性方面的进步。
- Slackware被提到作为后续使用的发行版，显示了其在早期用户中的流行程度。
- 总体来看，评论中对Linux早期发展的历史和个人体验充满怀旧感，并认可了这些早期发行版对Linux生态的贡献。

43923380.article_summary: Yggdrasil Linux/GNU/X（简称LGX）是由Yggdrasil Computing, Inc.开发的早期Linux发行版，该公司由Adam J. Richter于1992年在加州伯克利创立。它是首个基于Live CD的Linux发行版，自称是"即插即用"系统，能够自动配置硬件。Yggdrasil的发行版采用了Linux内核和GNU用户工具，默认界面为FVWM，遵循Unix文件系统层次标准（FHS）。首个alpha版本于1992年12月发布，包含了X Window System和多种GNU软件。1993年发布beta版，售价60美元，最终版售价99美元，但免费提供给软件被包含在发行版中的开发者。公司于1996年迁至圣何塞，2000年后逐渐停止活动，2004年公司状态被加州政府列为暂停。Yggdrasil对早期Linux的发展做出了重要贡献。

data.title: Heat stress mitigation by trees and shelters at bus stops
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：改善公共交通系统的舒适度以吸引和留住乘客

不同观点：
• ThinkBeat认为，增加公共交通工具的数量，特别是在高峰时段，以及改善车内降温设施，是提高乘客舒适度和吸引更多乘客的关键。
• elric则指出，许多城市正在试图降低公共交通成本，而不是增加舒适度，服务质量逐年下降，而价格却不断上涨。
• mhotchen将话题引向城市绿荫和天然遮蔽物的缺乏，认为这是人们需要使用防晒霜的原因。
• cadamsdotcom补充说，树木不仅能提供视觉上的放松，还能有效降温，比候车亭更凉爽。
• padjo反对砍伐树木，除非是为了防止树木倒塌的必要措施。
• lucidguppy提出利用Miyawaki方法，在有限空间内创造类似森林的环境。
• MattSayar提到现代遮阳设施（如遮阳篷）在降低温度方面的作用，并询问是否有外观现代的遮阳设计。
• MeteorMarc警告说，在气候变化和水资源短缺的情况下，树木可能因缺水而死亡或燃烧。
• mykowebhn关注为树木提供热应激缓解措施的必要性。
• tppiotrowski引用凤凰城的例子，指出种植和维护树木的高成本和挑战。
• newer_vienna对是否需要科学研究来证明树木和遮蔽物提供阴凉的常识性作用表示质疑。
• amunozo强调实现这些改进需要政治意愿。
• profsummergig通过对比特拉维夫和其他沙漠城市，说明城市绿化对生活质量的提升。
• JohnMakin描述加州反其道而行，拆除候车亭和长椅以防止无家可归者留宿，阻碍了改善候车环境的努力。
• nickdothutton幽默地建议英国市政当局可以考虑用金属树代替真实树木以降低维护成本。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的争议焦点包括城市在公共交通舒适度与成本控制之间的权衡，以及种植和维护树木的实际成本和可行性。
• 不同地区的政策差异也被提及，例如加州拆除候车设施以应对无家可归者问题的做法，与其他地区种植树木改善环境的努力形成对比。
• 技术和设计解决方案，如遮阳篷和Miyawaki方法，也被认为是提升城市生活质量的可行途径。

data.author: c16
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于L-band及其在科学和军事应用中的使用和干扰

不同观点：
• jjwiseman分享了关于使用科学传感器检测有意RF干扰的历史和例子，提到了多个推特帖子和地图链接，如AMSR和SMAP的应用。
• dakr指出SMAP任务的科学价值，强调其在地球科学和气候研究中的重要性，并提到其在水管理和农业方面的应用，同时也暗示了当前政府对此类科学任务的支持可能不足。
• drmpeg详细说明了1400到1427 MHz频段的分配情况，指出其专门用于射电天文学和被动地球探测卫星，并提到在美国1240到1400 MHz频段分配给雷达，GNSS下行链路在1240到1300 MHz之间不受保护。
• bob1029提到Iridium卫星利用L-band与地面站通信的功能，特别是在紧急情况下（如海难）的实用性。
• Alex-Programs讨论了L-band在现代战争中的战略重要性，包括干扰无人机和目标定位，并指出在冲突中，国际条约可能被忽视。

补充讨论：
• NoSalt对数据处理脚本中如何获取NASA SMAP数据文件表示疑问，不确定是通过API还是通过RTL-SDR直接获取。
• kevin_thibedeau插入了一个与主题无关的政治评论，提到克里米亚的领土争议。
• mellow_observer对俄罗斯干扰地点对应的重要位置表示困惑，试图理解这些地点为何需要无人机保护。
• logicziller询问是否有其他频段可以类似地进行观察。
• o_1对L-band的新发现表示赞赏。
• nanna请求用通俗语言解释讨论内容。
• x0询问是否有其他卫星接收有趣的频率，特别是6GHz以下的频段。
• g4zj质疑NASA是否意识到L-band干扰的问题。
• 4ad指出讨论未解答为何军方使用L-band，强调了解L-band对军方具体属性的重要性，而不仅仅是其是否被干扰。

争议焦点：
• L-band在军事和科学应用中的重要性以及在冲突中被故意干扰的现实。
• 对NASA SMAP数据文件获取方式的疑问和讨论。
• L-band在不同应用场景中的具体技术细节和用途。

data.title: How to harden GitHub Actions
data.author: moyer
data.article_summary: 本文总结了GitHub Actions相关的安全风险及其近期两个攻击事件。首先，去年12月，攻击者利用GitHub Actions漏洞在Ultralytics Python包中植入加密挖矿程序。随后，今年3月发生了“tj-actions”事件，攻击者利用多种反模式进行供应链攻击。具体步骤包括：利用spotbugs漏洞获取访问令牌，推送恶意工作流，泄露GitHub秘密，最终攻击tj-actions代码库。为防范此类风险，建议采取以下措施：1) 将工作流权限默认设为只读；2) 限制使用经过验证的Actions，并使用允许列表；3) 控制工作流的使用和限定运行器至特定代码库。这些措施旨在加强GitHub Actions的安全性，配合GitHub官方指南，提升代码安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub Actions的安全性及其使用中的潜在风险和解决方案

不同观点：
• [ebfe1] 提出了一种工具，用于将GitHub Actions中的版本替换为提交哈希，以提高安全性。该工具允许用户控制哪些操作需要固定版本，并提供了忽略某些来自知名组织的操作的选项。
• [20thr] 强调在其公司Namespace中，GitHub任务默认运行在受限的cgroup中，并且需要显式选择才能启用完全权限模式。他们认为多层保护是构建安全系统的关键。
• [cyrnel] 指出，尽管上述建议有帮助，但并没有解决tj-actions/changed-files问题的核心，即不必要的CAP_SYS_PTRACE权限导致的安全问题。建议通过限制依赖项的能力来减少风险。
• [RadiozRadioz] 质疑使用大量第三方Actions的必要性，并认为基础的构建和部署可以通过简单的脚本和容器完成，而不需要依赖过多的预制步骤。
• [duped] 批评GitHub Actions的设计缺乏锁定机制，建议引入类似现代包管理器的校验和验证功能，以防止安全漏洞。
• [newman314] 提到Step Security工具可以帮助保护GitHub Actions的安全性，并提供了一个链接。
• [kylegalbraith] 强调GitHub Actions面临多种安全风险，尤其是自托管 runner 的使用可能引入更多潜在风险，建议使用无持久性的runner来减少攻击面。
• [axelfontaine] 对自托管 runner 不应与公共仓库一起使用的观点提出异议，认为通过使用即时令牌和临时runner可以实现安全性。
• [cedws] 分享了在工作中审查第三方Actions时发现的危险做法，如运行未固定的安装脚本，并表示正在开发内部替代方案。
• [tomrod] 表示支持广泛使用GitHub Actions，但对其供应链攻击的风险表示担忧。
• [wallrat] 提到正在关注一个项目ghasum，它可以为所有Actions创建可验证的校验和清单。
• [bob1029] 强调最安全的GitHub Action是尽量不使用，并指出过于复杂的权限配置容易导致安全问题。
• [diggan] 认为在使用第三方Actions时，审查代码本身比依赖流行度或其他指标更为重要。
• [MadsRC] 分享了一个用于检测和修复未固定依赖项的CLI工具，并提到正在开发递归扫描功能。
• [DGAP] 提到一个开源的沙箱工具bullfrogsec，认为其对保护GitHub Actions有帮助。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于如何有效保护GitHub Actions的安全性，包括是否应使用第三方Actions、如何处理权限配置、是否需要固定版本及校验和机制等。
• 不同工具和方法被提及，如自动替换哈希的工具、cgroup限制、沙箱工具和校验和清单等，显示出社区对解决安全问题的多样化尝试。
• 自托管runner的使用及其潜在风险也被广泛讨论，强调了无持久性和最小权限原则的重要性。

43901190.article_content:
Wiz
Pricing
Get a demo
Get a demo
Over
the past three years
, researchers have highlighted the risks associated with GitHub Actions. These threats became manifest with two recent incidents.
First,
last December brought a supply chain attack
where attackers exploited a vulnerable GitHub Actions workflow to introduce an XMRig cryptominer to deployment versions of the Ultralytics Python package. Then, in March, we had the “tj-actions" incident. The attacker in this incident took advantage of multiple common anti-patterns associated with GitHub Actions and clearly leveraged the existing research literature to inform their tactics. An in-depth analysis of that incident is available in our blog posts:
GitHub Action tj-actions/changed-files supply chain attack: everything you need to know
New GitHub Action supply chain attack: reviewdog/action-setup
As a short recap:
A vulnerability in
spotbugs/sonar-findbugs
allowed an attacker to compromise the Personal Access Token (PAT) of a Spotbugs contributor
That compromised PAT was used to grant a temporary, malicious user
spotbugs/spotbugs
repository access
The write access to
spotbugs/spotbugs
was used to push a malicious workflow to a branch, leaking the Github secrets – including the PAT of a mutual
spotbugs
and
reviewdog
contributor
The
reviewdog
access was then used to briefly poison
reviewdog/action-setup@v1
, which allowed the attacker to further compromise a
tj-actions
PAT
The
tj-actions
access was used first to target Coinbase (unsuccessfully), and was then burned with a broad attack that changed all tj-actions versions to include malicious code
In the follow up to this incident, we know many organizations are investing in reviewing and hardening their GitHub Actions posture. We hope this guide serves as a cheat sheet for this complicated landscape, complementing
Github’s first party guidance
.
GitHub Actions: Essential Terminology
Based on data from Cardoen, G., Mens, T., & Decan, A. (2024). A dataset of GitHub Actions workflow histories
It’s important to establish the key terms relevant to this domain:
GitHub Actions
: A suite of automation features within GitHub that lets you automate tasks in your software development lifecycle. Actions can be used to build, test, and deploy code, among other things.
Workflow
: A collection of automated tasks, defined in a YAML file, that runs in response to specific events within your GitHub repository. Think of it as a script that automates a series of Actions. Workflows can be triggered by events like pushing code, creating a pull request, on a schedule, or on demand.
Action
: A reusable unit of automation that can be referenced and executed within Workflows. These can be created by you or pulled from the Marketplace and are essentially optional building blocks of Workflows. You can think of Actions like functions in a programming language—small, self-contained tasks that are reusable across Workflows.
Event
: The trigger that starts a Workflow. Common events include code pushes, pull request creations, or manual triggers.
Job
: A unit of work within a Workflow. Workflows can contain multiple Jobs, and each Job can run tasks (Actions). Jobs in a Workflow can run in parallel or sequentially, depending on how they're configured. Job is the minimal unit of execution schedulable on a runner.
Basically,
Workflows
are your automation scripts, which are built from the embedded
Job
code and referenced
Actions
.
Based on data from Cardoen, G., Mens, T., & Decan, A. (2024). A dataset of GitHub Actions workflow histories
Configuring GitHub for Safer GitHub Actions
Securing GitHub Actions starts with hardening your GitHub environment. First, secure GitHub Actions through organization-level administrative settings.
1. Set Read-Only Default Workflow Permissions
By default, the Workflow Token Permissions were set to
read-write
prior to February 2023
. For security reasons, it's crucial to set this to
read-only
. Write permissions allow Workflows to inadvertently or maliciously modify your repository and its data, making least-privilege crucial.
Double-check to ensure this permission is set correctly to
read-only
in your repository settings.
Source: Wiz's 2025 State of Code Security Report
2. Limit Actions to Verified Actions and an Allowlist
One of the key security measures is to
control which Actions can run within your Workflows
. You can restrict Workflows to only use
verified Actions
from trusted sources. This includes:
Actions created by GitHub
: These are Actions maintained and supported by GitHub itself.
Actions from Marketplace-verified creators
: Actions from verified creators in the GitHub Marketplace are more trustworthy, as they have undergone some level of review.
You can then use an allowlist of specific other trusted or reviewed Actions to extend permitted sources.
3. Govern Workflow Adoption and Restrict Runners to Specific Repositories

43901190.article_summary: 本文总结了GitHub Actions相关的安全风险及其近期两个攻击事件。首先，去年12月，攻击者利用GitHub Actions漏洞在Ultralytics Python包中植入加密挖矿程序。随后，今年3月发生了“tj-actions”事件，攻击者利用多种反模式进行供应链攻击。具体步骤包括：利用spotbugs漏洞获取访问令牌，推送恶意工作流，泄露GitHub秘密，最终攻击tj-actions代码库。为防范此类风险，建议采取以下措施：1) 将工作流权限默认设为只读；2) 限制使用经过验证的Actions，并使用允许列表；3) 控制工作流的使用和限定运行器至特定代码库。这些措施旨在加强GitHub Actions的安全性，配合GitHub官方指南，提升代码安全。

data.title: Egyptologist uncovers hidden messages on Paris’s iconic obelisk
data.author: isaacfrond
data.article_summary: 巴黎协和广场的埃及方尖碑上发现隐藏的象形文字信息。埃及学家Jean-Guillaume Olette-Pelletier注意到这些加密象形文字，它们包含字谜或文字游戏，只有古埃及的知识精英才能解读。这些信息旨在强调法老拉美西斯二世是神灵指定的统治者，并声称其祖先来自阿蒙-拉和玛特。方尖碑原位于卢克索神庙外，其加密信息仅在特定角度对乘船抵达的贵族可见，旨在强化法老不可动摇的神权统治，是一种针对精英的宣传。方尖碑在2024年巴黎奥运会前进行清理时得到了近距离研究确认。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于古埃及方尖碑上的信息是否属于加密信息，及其相关背景的讨论

不同观点：
• **[helpfulclippy]** 认为方尖碑上的信息不应被视为加密信息。他指出，信息内容简单直接，如“神-王不可废黜”、“向神献祭”等，且由于方尖碑较高，顶部的文字只能从远处阅读，因此更像是一种装饰性排版，而非真正的加密。

• **[Luc]** 引用了法语文章，提到图坦卡蒙宝座上的人物四肢姿态隐藏着象形文字信息，且只有极少数专家能解码。他质疑这些观点是否为主流学术界所接受。

• **[Trasmatta]** 提到纽约中央公园的方尖碑，认为其与巴黎的方尖碑相似，并关注气候对文物的损害问题。

• **[DemocracyFTW2]** 强调古代埃及艺术中文字与图像的结合，指出所谓的“象形文字加密”实际上是图像和文字的结合使用，而非真正的加密。他以拉美西斯二世的雕像为例，说明古埃及艺术家的高度语言和艺术意识。

• **[nunobrito]** 认为新闻文章有“标题党”嫌疑，因为方尖碑上的信息并非秘密，只是位于面向河流的一侧，乘船者更容易看到，而非步行者。

补充讨论：
• **对文物归还的讨论**：[BurnGpuBurn] 和 [amitport] 提到了方尖碑和其他文物的归还问题，质疑这些文物是否应归还原属国。

• **讨论的偏题**：[DemocracyFTW2] 指出讨论被转移到与方尖碑文字无关的政治问题上，认为归还问题虽然重要但与方尖碑上的文字讨论无关。

争议焦点：
• 方尖碑上的信息是否属于加密信息，还是仅仅是艺术表现和普通象形文字的使用。
• 文物归还问题在讨论中的相关性。

Dr. Jean-Guillaume Olette-Pelletier examining the obelisk
PARIS, FRANCE—
Artnet
reports that on his daily walks around Paris, Egyptologist Jean-Guillaume Olette-Pelletier of Paris Sorbonne University and Institut Catholique de Paris began to notice unusual hieroglyphics on the giant obelisk standing in the city’s Place de la Concorde. The monument was erected during the reign of Ramesses II (reigned ca. 1279–1213
b.c.
) and originally stood outside Egypt’s Luxor Temple, but was moved to France in the 1830s. Olette-Pelletier believed that the carved stone block could feature crypto-hieroglyphics, secret messages involving puzzles or wordplay that only Egypt’s educated and intellectual elite would have been able to read. He was given the opportunity to examine the 70-foot obelisk up close as it underwent cleaning prior to the 2024 Paris Olympics, and confirmed that the symbols did indeed contain at least seven examples of crypto-hieroglyphics. These essentially sought to remind those who could read them that Ramesses II had been chosen by the gods and claimed his ancestry from Amun-Re and Maat. Their location on the stone would have only made them visible to nobles who arrived at the Luxor Temple by boat during the Opet festival, which was held annually during the Nile's flood season and reinforced the pharaoh's right to rule. “Given the angle of approach, the nobility would have seen the hidden message and reflected: ‘the king confirms himself as god incarnate, who cannot be dethroned,'” Olette-Pelletier said. “It was propaganda aimed at the very high intellectual elite.” To read about obelisks from the Egyptian city of Heliopolis that were later moved to European cities, go to "
Egypt's Eternal City
."

data.title: How Obama’s BlackBerry got secured (2013)
data.author: lastdong
data.article_summary: 2009年，奥巴马就任美国总统时，因安全风险被迫放弃使用黑莓手机，引发广泛关注。虽然初期有报道称他完全放弃黑莓，但实际上在经过特殊加密和安全措施后，他得以继续使用。其前任小布什在2000年上任时也放弃了使用电子邮件。奥巴马的黑莓经过美国特勤局、白宫通信局和国家安全局的多方协作，安装了加密软件SecurVoice，以确保通信安全。初期曾考虑使用军用设备Sectéra Edge，但因其笨重不便而未被奥巴马采纳。最终，奥巴马保留了一部经过安全强化的黑莓手机，并更改了电子邮件地址以确保保密。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于政府和军队高层的安全通信设备及其安全性的讨论，特别是对黑莓设备及其技术细节的分析，以及对现代安全通信方案的争议。

不同观点：
• bigfatkitten：介绍NSA的商业解决方案（CSfC）用于保护移动通信，尤其是通过多层加密来保护涉密信息。同时指出，虽然CNSA算法足够强大，但实施不当或操作失误仍可能导致风险。CSfC通过使用来自不同来源的两个或多个加密层来降低单一漏洞危及整个系统的风险。

• miki123211：指出关于黑莓设备的技术细节在互联网上非常稀缺，尤其是其操作系统和通信协议。与iOS、Android等现代操作系统，甚至Symbian等老旧系统相比，黑莓的技术细节几乎无法获取，只有一些黑客会议和旧书中的信息。

• metadat：通过archive.org恢复了一些关于Sectera Edge（类似于黑莓的超安全PDA手机）的旧链接，并指出这些设备的分析和拆解会很有趣，但设备难以获得。

• evanjrowley：回忆起十年前见过政府使用的安全黑莓设置，并提到承包商具有深厚的机构知识，可能一生只做这一项工作。
